ProjectSpecification__Description: Project specification notes for the TrueVision drawings. Groups hold notes in order; a note’s code is its group’s prefix and its place in the group (GN01, EE02), so the order is the truth and Note__Code is written for readers and recomputed on every load. Specification bubbles on the Layout Editor sheets link to notes by Note__Id. General groups are listed on every sheet’s notes margin, after the notes that sheet’s bubbles link to. LastIdNumber only ever goes up, so no id is used twice.

Group__Notes.Note__Body: Working name Juggles Joint: planned home of James and Laura. Central section of the two-storey Lincolnshire stone barn, including the hay-barn-style front extension at the centre of the long elevation. Five brick arches; retention intended.

Working name Boutique Airbnb: short-term let providing rental income for the Sharpe and Watchorn households. East flank of the two-storey barn, the section that returns around the corner. Oak king-post trusses to be restored; double-height spaces. Existing double-height barn opening in the east elevation to be infilled with a large arched glazed opening.

Smallest unit, at the west end of the barn: cottage for sale. If funds are limited, option to complete as a watertight shell for later use or sale. Size unknown until the division with Unit 1 is set; James to decide from the area plans showing approximate gross floor area of each unit.
Original farmhouse of the farmstead, home of the Sharpe family. A substantial existing dwelling.

TO BE REMOVED. Simple framed agricultural barn with timber cladding and an asbestos-cement roof. Roof: dual-pitched section and lean-to, split approximately one-third and two-thirds of the length. Large central opening for agricultural machinery.
TO BE REMOVED. Large open barn, used mainly for vehicle storage. Low-pitched roof of rusted corrugated sheeting. Stone walls enclose the east side; open to the courtyard on the west side.

TO BE REMOVED. Single-storey range of agricultural sheds and stores, running north to south along the west flank of the barn. Two-thirds slate-roofed to match the two-storey barn; one-third dilapidated, near-flat corrugated sheeting. Structure failing. Unlike SP05 and SP06, part of the original barn. Ask the LPA whether conversion of at least the slate-roofed part is preferred. That part could give Unit 3 courtyard-facing kitchen accommodation if James takes more of the central courtyard.

View north from the arches of the barn's north elevation. Ground falls approximately 30 m towards the main road, with a view into the valley; fall to be confirmed by survey. Trees and the transformer at SP09 obstruct the view: tree removal and relocation of the transformer discussed. Glazing proposed between the arches, to the Unit 1 main kitchen.

Approximate location of the existing electrical transformer, mounted on a tall pylon. Not surveyed by Noble Architecture. Ownership, public or private, and extent of the infrastructure unknown. Engage a specialist before any relocation; costs may be significant. Noble Architecture accepts no responsibility for its location or for any consequences of removing or relocating it.

Main access road into the central farmstead; the farm holding is much larger. This end stretch runs east to west around the corner of the barn, then north to south past the Sharpe Residence to a parking area.

Courtyard between the barn ranges: heavily overgrown and derelict. Strip back and clear the whole area. Survey unreliable here: vegetation blocked the photogrammetry images, so much of this area is estimated. Resurvey the whole area after clearance.
Driveway running north to south along the east side of the Sharpe Residence, between the house and the barn's single-storey west range at SP07. Continues down to SP13 and SP14.
Main driveway and parking for the Sharpe Residence.
Tall agricultural barn, presumed still in active use; use unknown. Outside the proposed works. Marked for reference only; no measurements taken.
